title: Houston, TX: Space City meets food paradise — BBQ, Viet-Cajun crawfish, world-class museums, and Texas-sized hospitality
description: Four days exploring America's most diverse food city. From NASA's Mission Control to the sprawling Chinatown, legendary BBQ joints, and the electric nightlife of Montrose — Houston rewards the curious and the hungry.

days.title: Space City & Southern Smoke
days.description: Start with Houston's crown jewel — NASA — then ease into the city with legendary BBQ and downtown evening vibes.

activities.name: Check into Hotel ZaZa (Museum District)
activities.description: Base yourselves in the Museum District for walkability to Hermann Park, restaurants, and the light rail. Mid-range group suites work great for 5+. NASA's official visitor center is a must. The Level 9 tour gets you behind-the-scenes access to Mission Control and astronaut training. Budget 3-4 hours — the tram tour to see the Saturn V rocket is worth the wait.

activities.name: Evening at Discovery Green
activities.description: Walk off dinner at this 12-acre downtown park. Summer brings free outdoor concerts and movie screenings. The misting features help with the heat.

days.title: Chinatown Deep Dive & Montrose Vibes
days.description: Dive into Houston's incredible Asian food scene in the morning, then explore the colorful, eclectic Montrose neighborhood by evening.

activities.name: Menil Collection & Rothko Chapel
activities.description: One of the best free art museums in America. The Rothko Chapel next door is a stunning meditative octagonal space with 14 Mark Rothko paintings. Both free, both air-conditioned — perfect morning culture hit.

activities.name: Explore Houston Chinatown
activities.description: One of the largest Chinatowns in the US, sprawling along Bellaire Blvd. Hit 99 Ranch Market or H Mart for snacks, browse Hong Kong City Mall, grab boba at Tiger Sugar. A full sensory experience.

activities.name: Montrose Mural Walk & Shopping
activities.description: Walk along Westheimer to see Houston's best street art. Pop into Cactus Music (legendary vinyl shop), vintage stores, and quirky boutiques. Houston's most colorful, eclectic neighborhood.

days.title: Museums, BBQ & Heights Nightlife
days.description: Spend the day between world-class museums and Houston's best BBQ, then explore the charming Heights neighborhood into the evening.

activities.name: Stroll 19th Street in The Heights
activities.description: Houston's most charming neighborhood street. Browse vintage shops, local boutiques, and antique stores. The Victorian-era bungalows are beautiful. Great for a morning walk before peak heat.

activities.name: Houston Museum of Natural Science
activities.description: The paleontology hall is jaw-dropping — one of the best dinosaur collections in the country. The gems and minerals vault is stunning. Budget 2-3 hours. Fully air-conditioned, perfect for the afternoon heat.

activities.name: Hermann Park & Miller Outdoor Theatre
activities.description: Stroll Houston's crown jewel park as evening cools. The Japanese Garden is serene. Check if Miller Outdoor Theatre has a free performance — the summer schedule is packed with concerts, plays, and dance.

days.title: Gulf Coast Flavors & Farewell
days.description: Soak in the last of Houston's highlights — a morning bayou walk, the iconic Water Wall, and one final legendary BBQ stop before heading home.

activities.name: Buffalo Bayou Park
activities.description: Take an early morning walk or rent bikes along the bayou before heat peaks. The Johnny Steele Dog Park is fun, and 250,000 bats emerge from under the Waugh Bridge at dusk! Beautiful urban green space.

activities.name: Gerald D. Hines Waterwall Park
activities.description: This 64-foot semicircular fountain is one of Houston's most iconic photo spots. The rushing water creates a dramatic, meditative effect. Quick stop but absolutely worth it.

activities.name: Check Out & Depart
activities.description: Head to George Bush Intercontinental (IAH, 30-45 min) or Hobby Airport (HOU, 20 min from Museum District). Leave extra time — Houston traffic is real, especially in summer.
